title: 1968 Indian Air Force An-12 crash
summary: Indian Air Force An-12 Flight 203, flown by Flight Lieutenant Harkewal Singh and Squadron Leader Pran Nath Malhotra, was on approach to Leh from Chandigarh when the pilot turned back due to inclement weather; the aircraft went missing with its last radio contact over the Rohtang Pass and was declared lost after searches failed to find the wreck. Expeditions between 2003 and 2024 have recovered remains and wreckage from Himalayan glaciers, confirming the aircraft went down in terrain at about 18,000 ft.

factors.evidence: the pilot decided to turn back due to inclement weather
the aircraft then went missing with the last radio contact over the Rohtang Pass
The crash location lies at a height of about 18,000 ft, at a gradient of 80 degrees

events.text: Flight 203 was on approach to Leh when the pilot decided to turn back due to inclement weather.
The aircraft went missing, with the last radio contact over the Rohtang Pass, and was declared missing after the failure to find the wreck.
On 18 August 2019, a joint Indian Army and Air Force team recovered aircraft parts including the aero engine, fuselage, propeller and a cockpit door.

notes: No formal investigation finding stated; aircraft was missing for decades, only wreckage/remains recovered.

title: Air France 212 (1968)
summary: Air France Flight 212, a Boeing 707 on a scheduled service from Santiago to Paris, crashed on 6 March 1968 while approaching Le Raizet Airport in Pointe-à-Pitre, Guadeloupe. The aircraft was cleared for a visual approach and began descent from 9,000 feet, but struck Grande Découverte mountain at 3,937 feet, killing all 63 occupants. Accident investigators determined the probable cause was initiation of a nighttime visual approach from an incorrectly identified point.
probable_cause: Initiation of a nighttime visual approach from an incorrectly identified point

initiation of a nighttime visual approach

Continuing on a northwesterly course, aircraft descended at decreasing altitude
Aircraft struck Grande Découverte mountain at an altitude of 3,937 feet

notes: Clear probable cause established by BEA investigation

title: Aer Lingus 712
summary: Flight 712 crashed into the sea off Tuskar Rock, County Wexford, on March 24, 1968, killing all 61 passengers and crew. The aircraft was proceeding normally until a call was heard with probable contents twelve thousand feet descending spinning rapidly; thereafter no further radio contact was established. Investigation lasted two years but a definitive cause was never determined. A 2002 review concluded the crash was likely caused by a chain of events starting with flutter-induced fatigue failure of the elevator trim tab mechanism, though other theories including bird strike or structural failure from corrosion were also proposed.
probable_cause: Likely consequence of a chain of events starting with a failure to the left tail-plane caused by metal fatigue, corrosion, flutter, or a bird strike, with the most likely cause being a flutter-induced fatigue failure of the elevator trim tab operating mechanism.

title: South African Airways 228
summary: South African Airways Flight 228, a new Boeing 707 taking off from Windhoek on 20 April 1968 in a dark, moonless night with no ground lights, initially climbed to 650 ft then leveled off and started to descend. Fifty seconds after takeoff the aircraft flew into terrain at approximately 271 knots. The crew failed to maintain safe airspeed and altitude by not observing flight instruments.
probable_cause: The captain and first officer failed to maintain a safe airspeed and altitude and a positive climb by not observing flight instruments during takeoff. Loss of situational awareness in dark, moonless night conditions contributed; the crew misread altitude and vertical speed indicators.

factors.evidence: It was a dark, moonless night with few, if any, lights on the ground in the open desert
The crew had no visual reference in the dark, leading to spatial disorientation
they failed to maintain a safe airspeed and altitude and a positive climb by not observing flight instruments
The aircraft initially climbed to an altitude of 650 ft above ground level, then leveled off and started to descend
Fifty seconds after take-off, it flew into the ground in flight configuration at a speed of approximately 271 kn
the manufacturer subsequently recognised the lack of a ground proximity warning system in its aircraft

events.text: The aircraft took off from Windhoek on runway 08 at 18:49 GMT into a dark, moonless night.
The aircraft initially climbed to an altitude of 650 ft above ground level, then leveled off.
The aircraft began to descend while the crew had no visual reference in the dark conditions.
Fifty seconds after take-off, the aircraft flew into the ground in flight configuration at approximately 271 knots.
The aircraft's four engines were the first parts to touch the ground, creating four deep gouges in the soil.
Two fires erupted immediately when the aircraft's fuel tanks ignited.

title: 1968 Kham Duc C-130 shootdown
summary: A USAF C-130B commanded by Major Bernard L. Bucher was shot down on 12 May 1968 while evacuating civilians from the besieged Kham Duc camp. After landing under fire and loading 150 evacuees, Bucher took off northward, unaware North Vietnamese forces were concentrated there; under fire from 12.7mm and 14.5mm heavy machine guns the aircraft shook violently out of control and crashed into a ravine less than a mile from the airstrip, killing everyone aboard.

factors.evidence: under intense anti-aircraft fire from 12.7mm and 14.5mm heavy machine guns
the aircraft ... shook violently out of control, crashed into a nearby ravine

events.text: The C-130 approached the Kham Duc airstrip from the south and managed to land despite taking hits from North Vietnamese forces during the battle.
As soon as it landed, 150 South Vietnamese evacuees rushed onto the aircraft until it was full.
Major Bucher took off in a northward direction, unaware that North Vietnamese forces were concentrated in that area.

Under intense anti-aircraft fire from 12.7mm and 14.5mm heavy machine guns, the aircraft shook violently out of control and crashed into a ravine less than a mile from the airstrip, killing everyone aboard.

notes: Account is based on eyewitness reports cited in the article; no formal investigation report is referenced.
The text's breakdown of 150 evacuees, 1 Special Forces officer and 5 crew (156) is one more than the item's recorded death toll of 155.

title: Air France 1611
summary: Air France Flight 1611, a Sud Aviation Caravelle, took off from Ajaccio at 10:09 on 11 September 1968, bound for Nice. The flight was initially without incident and weather conditions were sunny. At 10:30 local time, on descending between flight level 90 to flight level 70, the flight crew declared an emergency mentioning a fire on board. The radio and radar contact was lost after a final contact at 10:33, and a kerosene slick and floating debris were discovered, confirming that the plane had crashed into the sea with all 95 people aboard.
probable_cause: The report surmised that the loss of the aircraft was caused by a fire in the passenger toilet caused either by a defective water heater or a cigarette discarded in a waste bin. The direct cause of loss of control could not be definitively established: it may be related to the pilots' physical incapacity caused either by toxic gas emissions or by passengers invading the cockpit.

factors.evidence: Fire originated in the rear passenger toilet, caused either by a defective water heater or a cigarette discarded in a waste bin.

The direct cause of loss of control could not be definitively established: it may be related to the pilots' physical incapacity caused either by toxic gas emissions or by passengers invading the cockpit.
Fire propagated until the aircraft control was lost.
The radio and radar contact was lost, and the aircraft crashed into the Mediterranean Sea.

events.text: The Caravelle took off from Ajaccio at 10:09, and the first part of the flight was without incident with sunny weather conditions.
On descending between flight level 90 to flight level 70, the flight crew declared an emergency mentioning a fire on board.
The radio and radar contact was lost after a final contact at 40-45 km from Nice.
A kerosene slick and floating debris were discovered in the Mediterranean Sea, confirming that the plane had crashed into the sea.

title: Pan Am 217
summary: Pan Am Flight 217, a Boeing 707, crashed into the Caribbean Sea near Caracas at 22:05 local time while nearing Caracas on approach from New York. The crew was caught by an optical illusion created by the lights of the city on an upslope. All 51 passengers and crew perished. The aircraft disappeared from radar and crashed into the Caribbean Sea, with wreckage found 11.4 miles from Caracas.
probable_cause: Pilot error resulting from an optical illusion created by the lights of the city of Caracas on an upslope caused the crew to descend until they crashed into the sea.
